title: runstate v0.4 lifecycle convention
description: Pins the bodies of the lifecycle.* topics the worker produces: started (attach + self-reported liveness handle), heartbeat (tick beacon), stopped (cooperative dying breath), nak (a refused control request). Applied on top of the envelope schema. v0.4 dates the beacon (docs/specs/observer-clock.md): started/heartbeat/stopped gain a REQUIRED, non-null `t` -- the emitter's wall-clock at emission, the clock a third-party observer reads for freshness (seq orders, t measures; t is never an ordering key). The beacon (heartbeat) is exactly the record liveness reads, and a beacon with no time cannot do its one job; the emitter always knows now, so t is required, never fabricated (no default). nak stays undated -- it is not read by the observer plane.

Started.description: Pushed on attach; the worker self-reports its liveness handle (§8). t is the worker's wall-clock when it emitted the record -- required non-null (a worker that attaches always attaches at a time; the run epoch memoizer._epoch reads). Renamed from v0.3's present-nullable `attached_at`, harmonized with its heartbeat/stopped siblings (observer-clock §3, §10).

Heartbeat.description: Tick-driven liveness beacon. consumed_seq is the worker's read position in its inbound `control` order (§11-12), published after durable registration. t is the worker's wall-clock at the beat -- required non-null; the record liveness reads, so it dates the newest beacon for any third-party observer (observer-clock §2).

Stopped.description: The cooperative dying breath; its existence on the log = a clean, resumable halt (§7). completed=true is the worker's opt-in claim of intrinsic completion; otherwise the stop projects to preempted. error is the failure diagnostic; a completed stop carries no error. t is the worker's wall-clock at the halt -- required non-null; the finish-time and GC-age answer for a cleanly-stopped run (observer-clock §3, §6).

Nak.description: A refused control request, correlated by request_id. `reason` is a closed enum: malformed (body didn't conform -- a sender bug), unsatisfiable (well-formed but provably zero fires), unsupported (unknown control verb). `message` is free human detail. Undated: not read by the observer plane, kept minimal (observer-clock §3).
